## Lineage

**Basis [Record]:** Birutė's Palanga origin is a strong Lithuanian tradition (Birutė Hill, her role as a *vaidilutė* guarding a sacred fire). Długosz has her drowned in 1382; Lithuanian tradition has her living to c. 1416. Everything else is invention. The gift runs through the **mothers**, and each generation gives one daughter to the shore flame. [Birutė](../characters/birute.qmd) is the last vessel. Her maternal kin stay unnamed and few; a grandmother who was a vessel before her is the cleanest invention. The tradition that Birutė's relatives were killed in 1382 can mean that Jogaila's men tried to end the line (source to verify).

## Feuds & alliances

Allied to the Kęstutaičiai by Birutė's marriage; patron of [Kęstutaičiai](../factions/kestutaiciai.qmd) through the Amber Queen. Opposed in the saga by the Polish clergy who come to break the statue in 1417–18.

## Fate across the books

- **VI:** Birutė is chosen; the "abduction" (*Būk paimta*) places the Amber Queen's vessel in the Gediminid bed; Vytautas is born under the three spinners.
- **I:** Birutė becomes the Queen (1384); the kneeling amber statue stands at Palanga ([the pebble](../artifacts/pebble.qmd); [the statue](../artifacts/kneeling_woman.qmd)).
- **IV:** the clergy try to break the idol; their boat goes down.
- **V:** a remnant of women keeps a hidden fire without a vessel. The statue no longer glows in 1445 (ch. 25) and the sea takes it in 1450 (ch. 29).
